question: In the pyrolysis of teak tree leaves, why did the bio-oil yield keep rising all the way up to 500 °C?
expect: premise false: bio-oil rose from 300 to 450 °C, then decreased at 500 °C (p3)
rendered:
The question assumes that the bio-oil yield kept rising all the way up to 500 °C, which is not supported by the document. According to the document, the bio-oil yield increased as the pyrolysis temperature increased from 300 to 450 °C, but then decreased at 500 °C.

Document 1 does not provide a clear explanation for why the bio-oil yield decreased at 500 °C, but it suggests that the maximum bio-oil yield of 38.41% was achieved at 450°C for 25 minutes.

Therefore, the answer to the question is that the bio-oil yield did not keep rising all the way up to 500 °C.
